'''Walther Franz Anton von Dyck''' (6 December 1856 – 5 November 1934), born '''Dyck''' ({{IPA|de|diːk}}<ref>Pronunciation according to information from the [https://www.tum.de/en/about-tum/our-university/tum-board-of-management Board of Management of the Technical University of Munich].</ref>) and later [[von|ennobled]], was a German [[mathematician]]. He is credited with being the first to define a mathematical [[group (mathematics)|group]], in the modern sense in {{Harv|Dyck|1882}}. He laid the foundations of [[combinatorial group theory]],<ref name="stillwell374">{{Citation| publisher = Springer| isbn = 978-0-387-95336-6| last = Stillwell| first = John| title = Mathematics and its history| year = 2002| page = [https://books.google.com/books?id=WNjRrqTm62QC&pg=PA374 374]}}</ref> being the first to systematically study a group by [[Presentation of a group|generators and relations]].

==Biography==
[[File:Grabstaette Walther von Dyck.jpg|thumb|Bust of Walther von Dyck at his grave in Munich]]
Von Dyck was a student of [[Felix Klein]]<ref name="stillwell374"/> and served as chairman of the commission publishing [[Klein's encyclopedia]]. Von Dyck was also the editor of [[Johannes Kepler|Kepler's]] works.  He promoted technological education as rector of the [[Technische Hochschule of Munich]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Rowe|first=David E.|author-link=David E. Rowe|title=Review of ''Walther von Dyck (1856–1934). Mathematik, Technik und Wissenschaftsorganisation an der TH München''|journal=Historia Mathematica|date=November 2008|volume=35|issue=4|pages=333–334|doi=10.1016/j.hm.2008.08.002|doi-access=}}</ref> He was a Plenary Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1908 at Rome.<ref>{{cite book|author=Dyck, W. von|chapter= Die Encyklopädie der mathematischen Wissenschaften|editor=G. Castelnuovo|title=Atti del IV Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici (Roma, 6–11 Aprile 1908)|series= ICM proceedings|year=1909|volume=1|pages=123–134|publisher= University of Toronto Press|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0081.001;view=1up;seq=129}}</ref>

Von Dyck is the son of the Bavarian painter [[Hermann Dyck]].

==Legacy==
The [[Dyck language]] in formal language theory is named after him,<ref name="Udacity">{{Cite web |url=http://www.udacity.com/view#Course/cs262/CourseRev/apr2012/Unit/80001/Nugget/92002 |title=Udacity CS262 |access-date=2012-07-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227181339/https://www.udacity.com/view#Course/cs262/CourseRev/apr2012/Unit/80001/Nugget/92002 |archive-date=2016-12-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref> as are [[Dyck's theorem]] and [[Dyck's surface]] in the theory of [[surface (mathematics)|surface]]s, together with the [[von Dyck group]]s, the [[Dyck tessellation]]s, [[Dyck path]]s, and the [[Dyck graph]].
